sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: yellow versus yellow-green signs, triangle versus octagon, steady versus flashing lights, flashing red versus dark signals, sign families, bicycle, motorcycle and transit signals
Confusable pairs among the sign and signal rules, followed by continuation facts the main list did not hold; each block ties to one handbook page, all from the written text rather than the sign pictures, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Plain yellow signs cover road conditions and hazards in general, while fluorescent yellow-green signs focus on schools, pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds and school bus routes. [A01]
Why it matters: group sign colors; confusable yellow versus yellow-green.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
Orange signs flag temporary conditions such as work zones, whereas red signs carry regulations that require immediate action. [A01]
Why it matters: group sign colors; confusable orange versus red.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A02
A three-sided sign asks you to slow and be ready to stop in order to yield, but an eight-sided sign requires you to stop. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; confusable yield versus stop.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A02
A diamond sign is a hazard warning, while a rectangular sign may be a regulation, information or a warning such as an advisory curve speed, which is often paired with a diamond sign. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; confusable diamond versus rectangle.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A02
A round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead, whereas a five-sided sign warns of a school area. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; confusable circle versus pentagon.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A08
A flashing yellow light lets you go through with caution while cross traffic yields to you, but a flashing red requires a full stop first. [A08]
Why it matters: group flashing lights; confusable flashing yellow versus flashing red.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A08
A steady yellow light or arrow means your right of way is ending, while a flashing yellow arrow means you may turn after yielding. [A08]
Why it matters: group yellow signals; confusable steady versus flashing.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A08
At a flashing red where cross traffic does not have to stop, you may go only when the intersection is clear and you will not interfere with cross traffic. [A08]
Why it matters: group flashing red; confusable two-way versus all-way stop.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A08
If your light turns red while you are in the middle of the intersection, you may complete your turn once oncoming traffic has stopped. [A08]
Why it matters: group red signals; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A08
A rectangular rapid flashing beacon is a yellow flashing light at a crosswalk that flashes only after a pedestrian activates it. [A08]
Why it matters: group beacons; confusable with pedestrian hybrid beacon.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A01
The manual says seven background colors are commonly used on signs and that knowing the signs is needed to get an Indiana driver's license. [A01]
Why it matters: group sign colors; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A02
The manual lists seven common sign shapes, each pointing to a type of message. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A03
Warning signs as a family prepare drivers for road conditions and hazards ahead. [A03]
Why it matters: group sign families; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A04
Orange construction signs mainly warn of work zones, but some give guidance such as detours or state rules such as added penalties in a worksite. [A04]
Why it matters: group work zones; link to safe operation chapter.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A05
Traffic regulation signs control speed and movement and show rules drivers must obey, and speed advisory signs may be mounted with some warning signs. [A05]
Why it matters: group sign families; confusable regulation versus advisory.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A06
A supplemental plaque under a stop sign shows which directions at that intersection must stop. [A06]
Why it matters: group stop signs; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A06
Traffic guidance signs tell drivers the type of road, upcoming entrances and exits, and distances to destinations. [A06]
Why it matters: group sign families; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A07
Driver services and recreation signs tell drivers about nearby amenities, parks and recreation areas. [A07]
Why it matters: group sign families; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A09
A signal showing only bicycle symbols controls a bike lane or path and applies only to bicyclists, using red for stop, yellow for ending right of way and green for go. [A09]
Why it matters: group special signals; confusable bicycle versus vehicle signal.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A09
A bicyclist held at a red bicycle signal that will not change may proceed after stopping completely for at least two minutes and using due caution. [A09]
Why it matters: group special signals; difficulty high.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A09
A motorcycle or motor driven cycle stuck at a red signal may go through after a complete stop of at least two minutes with due caution, but this does not apply to autocycles. [A09]
Why it matters: group special signals; confusable motorcycle versus autocycle.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A09
A signal of white rectangular bars controls a bus or transit lane and applies only to bus or transit operators. [A09]
Why it matters: group special signals; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A09
Before pulling into a street from an alley or driveway, stop and yield to other vehicles. [A09]
Why it matters: group right of way; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0040]

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.
